findings.body: When `wsl --status` reports default version 1, this branch calls `wsl --install --no-distribution`. Microsoft documents that `--no-distribution` applies when WSL is not installed; changing an existing default requires `wsl --set-default-version 2`. The script can therefore finish without switching that laptop to WSL2, and rerunning it repeats the same command. [Microsoft WSL commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/basic-commands).
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — enable WSL2 when WSL1 is already installed

findings.body: The generated `npm.cmd` stub ends with a `findstr` check for Codex and has no successful `exit /b 0`. During the Claude Code install, that last check does not match and leaves a nonzero exit code, so the installer throws and the test's full-run assertion fails. This test is included in the Windows suite by `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23,35`. Make the stub return success after handling either package.
findings.title: Not done: Windows installer test runs in CI

findings.body: The plan requires the worker's functional check to record stubbed runs of both scripts. The head commit records Mac results but says the local Mac cannot report the Windows CI result; it provides no observed Windows outcome for the piped install, all-present path, or WSL2 guidance. The broken Windows test fixture also prevents that test from supplying the claimed result.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: Any directory with each browser prefix counts as installed, including an incomplete download or a revision incompatible with the Playwright version a project uses. The Windows script has the same check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:21`. Check mode can report nothing missing while tests cannot launch a browser. [Playwright requires version-specific browser binaries](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers).
findings.title: Check usable Playwright revisions before skipping installation

findings.body: A standalone `docker` command makes this branch skip the Docker Desktop cask; Windows uses the same command-only test at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:50`. That laptop can still lack the Desktop engine needed for prototype tests. Check for a usable Desktop installation or tell the user how to start it.
findings.title: Treat a Docker CLI without Docker Desktop as missing
